title: 11-schedule-builder-desktop-en
prompt: Design the SCHEDULE BUILDER — the centerpiece admin screen, desktop 1440px wide. Reuse the exact app shell from the source design (60px left icon rail with Schedule now ACTIVE, and the identical top bar). PAGE HEADER: title 'Schedule' 28/600, a Day/Week segmented toggle with Week active, a department selector showing 'FOH' with a BOH option, a '4 Warnings' amber pill button with a warning icon, a secondary 'Generate with AI' button with a sparkle icon, and a primary #2563EB 'Publish schedule' button at the far right. Beneath, a week navigator: left/right chevrons around 'Aug 10 – Aug 16, 2026' with a 'Today' ghost button. GRID HEADER ROW: a fixed 220px left column header reading 'Employee', then seven equal day columns headed 'MON 10, TUE 11, WED 12, THU 13, FRI 14, SAT 15, SUN 16' — each with the weekday in 11px/600 uppercase #6B7280 and the date in 15px/600 #1F2937, plus a small forecast line beneath in 11px #6B7280 reading 'Fcst 42, Fcst 45, Fcst 51, Fcst 58, Fcst 74, Fcst 82, Fcst 47' respectively. GRID BODY grouped by SHIFT ROLE: each group starts with a full-width colored BAND row — the role color at 12 percent opacity, with the role name uppercase 11px/600 letter-spaced in the full-strength color at the left, and a small hours total at the right. Show these groups in order: SERVER (#F5A623) with employee rows for Allison Rodriguez, Emily Roman, Rebekah Rosales, Micah Lozon; BARTENDER (#8B5CF6) with Isaac Boynton, Kevin Andricain; HOST (#F97316) with Daniela Zaragoza, Miley Estremera; RUNNER (#06B6D4) with Anthony; SHIFT SUPERVISOR (#22C55E) with Steph Fages, Val Sariol; MANAGER/MOD (#EC4899) with Daphne Jalil. Each employee row has a left cell with a 28px avatar, the name in 14px/500, and a 12px #6B7280 sub-line showing weekly hours like '28.5 hrs'. End each role group with a dashed ghost row '+ Add employee'. Also include an 'OPEN SHIFTS' row inside the Server group and inside the Bartender group, styled with a dashed border, showing one unassigned shift card each. SHIFT CARDS inside day cells: rounded-lg 8px, tinted with the role color at about 15 percent opacity with a 3px full-strength left border, containing the time on one line in 12px/600 tabular figures like '10:30a–4:00p', the station beneath in 11px #6B7280 like 'Floor' or 'Patio' or 'Bar' or 'Door', and a small square letter chip at the top-right showing S, H, or A. Populate the grid densely and realistically across all seven days — most employees work 4 to 5 shifts, weekends are fuller, and lunch shifts read 10:30a–4:00p while dinner shifts read 3:30p–10:00p. CONFLICT AND WARNING STATES, make these clearly visible: render ONE shift card with a red #FDE8E8 tint and a 1px #EF4444 border and a small red warning triangle in its corner — this is Micah Lozon on Thu Aug 13, an availability conflict; render a SECOND card with a small amber #F59E0B clock icon badge in its corner indicating an overtime warning — this is Isaac Boynton on Sat Aug 15; give one more card a small amber corner flag. FOOTER BAR pinned at the bottom, full width, white with a 1px top border: the left cell reads 'Labor' in 13px/600, then one cell per day aligned to the grid columns, each showing a small labor percentage pill on top and the hours and dollars beneath in 12px tabular figures — MON 44% 16.0 hrs $288, TUE 43% 17.0 hrs $302, WED 42% 18.5 hrs $330, THU 41% 20.0 hrs $358, FRI 39% 25.0 hrs $452, SAT 38% 27.0 hrs $486, SUN 45% 18.0 hrs $328. Percentage pills at or under 40% use the teal success tint, those above 42% use the amber warning tint. At the far right a bold week total block: 'Week total 141.5 hrs · $2,544 · 42.0%'. These numbers must match exactly. Use ONLY the fonts, colors, spacing and component styles in the design system; keep Inter, #1F2937 primary text, #6B7280 secondary text, and #2563EB for the only primary button. Never use the brand red #B4232A as a button color. No gradients, no serif or decorative typefaces. This grid must feel dense, scannable and operational like 7shifts, not airy or decorative.

title: 12-shift-modal-desktop-en
prompt: Design the ADD/EDIT SHIFT MODAL, desktop 1440px wide. Show the Schedule Builder grid behind it, dimmed with a 40 percent black scrim, so the context is obvious — the grid behind should match the source design's schedule styling with role bands and shift cards. The modal itself is 560px wide, centered, white, 16px radius, with a soft elevation shadow. MODAL HEADER: title 'Edit shift' 18/600, a 13px #6B7280 sub-line 'Saturday, Aug 15, 2026', and a close × at the right. BODY, a vertical stack of labeled fields with 13px/500 #6B7280 labels above each control: 1) 'Employee' — a select showing a 24px avatar plus 'Isaac Boynton'. 2) 'Shift role' — a select showing a purple Bartender chip; the select is open-adjacent so the role color dot is visible. 3) 'Station' — a select showing 'Bar'. 4) A two-column row: 'Start' showing '3:30 PM' and 'End' showing '11:00 PM', both time inputs with a small clock icon, times in tabular figures. 5) 'Required skill level' — a three-segment selector L1 / L2 / L3 with L2 selected in #2563EB; a 12px #6B7280 helper line beneath reads 'Only employees at or above this level can take or cover this shift.' 6) 'On-call shift' — a right-aligned toggle in the OFF state with the label at left and a 12px #6B7280 helper 'On-call staff are notified but not scheduled to arrive.' 7) 'Notes' — a textarea containing the realistic note 'Private party in the back room from 7 PM — expect a second bar setup.' ELIGIBLE EMPLOYEES PREVIEW: a bordered inner panel with heading 'Eligible employees' 13px/600 and a 12px #6B7280 caption 'Sorted by skill level', listing four rows each with a 24px avatar, name, a role chip, a small level badge, and availability text — Isaac Boynton · Bartender · L3 · Available (this row highlighted as the current pick), Kevin Andricain · Bartender · L2 · Available, Allison Rodriguez · Server · L2 · Can cover, Emily Roman · Server · L1 · Not eligible shown at 40 percent opacity with a small lock icon. FOOTER: a ghost 'Delete shift' in #EF4444 at the far left, then right-aligned white bordered 'Cancel' and primary #2563EB 'Save shift'. Use ONLY the design system's fonts, colors, spacing and components; keep Inter, #2563EB for the primary action, and never use brand red #B4232A as a button color. No gradients, no serif or decorative typefaces.

title: 13-schedule-ai-draft-desktop-en
prompt: Design the SCHEDULE BUILDER — AI DRAFT STATE, desktop 1440px wide. This is the same schedule grid as the source scheduling screen, with the identical app shell, role-band grouping, shift cards and labor footer — but in an unmistakable AI-generated, not-yet-published state. It must be obvious at a glance that NOTHING IS PUBLISHED. AI BANNER pinned directly under the page header, full width, violet-tinted background (#8B5CF6 at 10 percent opacity) with a 1px violet border and a 12px radius: a sparkle icon, the text 'AI draft — review required' in 15px/600 #1F2937, a sub-line in 13px #6B7280 reading 'Generated 2 minutes ago from availability, skill levels and forecast. Not visible to staff until you publish.', and at the right a white bordered 'Discard draft' button plus a primary #2563EB 'Accept as draft' button. Add a small violet 'AI DRAFT' pill next to the page title, and replace the usual Published state with a gray 'Draft' status pill. RATIONALE PANEL: a right-hand side panel about 320px wide, white with a 1px #E5E7EB border and 16px radius, docked beside the grid. Heading 'Why this schedule' 15px/600 with a sparkle icon. Then a list of rationale rows, each with a small teal check icon and 13px text: 'Balanced hours across servers — no one above 32 hrs', 'Robin Leyva off Saturday per approved time-off request', 'Friday bar coverage increased by 1 for the forecast of 74 covers', 'Micah Lozon kept off Thursday lunch to respect availability', 'Two L3 bartenders never scheduled on the same slow shift'. Beneath the list, a bordered stat strip showing 'Projected labor $2,544 · 42.0% · 141.5 hrs' in tabular figures with a 12px #6B7280 caption 'Within the 40% target on 3 of 7 days'. At the bottom of the panel a REGENERATE input: a label 'Adjust and regenerate' 13px/600, a textarea with the realistic placeholder 'e.g. give Emily more Friday hours and keep Sunday leaner', and a full-width secondary button 'Regenerate with instructions' carrying a sparkle icon. Every shift card in the grid should carry a subtle violet dashed outline to mark it as AI-proposed rather than confirmed, and the grid should still show the same realistic staffing, the one red availability-conflict card and the one amber overtime warning from the standard builder. Keep the labor footer identical: MON 44% 16.0 hrs $288, TUE 43% 17.0 hrs $302, WED 42% 18.5 hrs $330, THU 41% 20.0 hrs $358, FRI 39% 25.0 hrs $452, SAT 38% 27.0 hrs $486, SUN 45% 18.0 hrs $328, week total 141.5 hrs · $2,544 · 42.0%. Use ONLY the design system's fonts, colors, spacing and components. Violet #8B5CF6 appears here only as the AI-state accent and as the Bartender role color. Keep Inter and #2563EB for primary actions; never use brand red #B4232A as a button color. No gradients, no serif or decorative typefaces.

title: 15-publish-confirmation-desktop-en
prompt: Design the PUBLISH SCHEDULE CONFIRMATION MODAL, desktop 1440px wide, shown over the dimmed Schedule Builder grid with a 40 percent black scrim so the context is clear. Render TWO variants SIDE BY SIDE on the same frame, each clearly labeled above with a small 12px/600 uppercase #6B7280 caption — the left labeled 'FIRST PUBLISH' and the right labeled 'REPUBLISH — 3 EMPLOYEES AFFECTED'. Each modal is 520px wide, white, 16px radius, elevated. LEFT VARIANT, first publish: header 'Publish schedule' 18/600 with the sub-line 'Aug 10 – Aug 16, 2026' in 13px #6B7280 and a close ×. Body opens with a summary stat strip in a bordered inner panel: '46 shifts · 141.5 hrs · $2,544 projected labor · 42.0%' in tabular figures. Then a section headed 'What happens next' 13px/600 with three rows, each a teal check icon plus 13px text: '18 employees will be notified', 'Shifts become visible in the staff app immediately', 'Employees can request trades once published'. Then a NOTIFY block: a heading 'Notify by' 13px/600 with two checked checkboxes 'Push notification' and 'Email', and one unchecked 'SMS' shown at 40 percent opacity with a small 11px gray 'Coming soon' chip. Footer: white bordered 'Cancel' and primary #2563EB 'Publish schedule'. RIGHT VARIANT, republish: header 'Republish schedule' with an amber-tinted alert strip beneath reading 'This schedule was already published on Fri Aug 7 at 4:12 PM. Republishing will notify affected employees of the changes.' Body shows a CHANGES section headed 'Changes since last publish' 13px/600 with three rows, each an avatar plus a 13px description and a small change-type chip: Isaac Boynton — 'Sat Aug 15 · shift time changed 4:00p–11:00p to 3:30p–11:00p' with an amber 'Edited' chip; Emily Roman — 'Fri Aug 14 · new shift added 3:30p–10:00p Floor' with a teal 'Added' chip; Micah Lozon — 'Thu Aug 13 · shift removed' with a red 'Removed' chip. Beneath, a bordered strip in 13px reading '3 employees affected · 15 employees unchanged and will not be notified'. Footer: white bordered 'Cancel' and primary #2563EB 'Republish and notify 3'. Use ONLY the design system's fonts, colors, spacing and components; keep Inter and #2563EB for primary actions, teal #14B8A6 for added/approved, amber #F59E0B for edited/pending, red #EF4444 for removed. Never use brand red #B4232A as a button color. No gradients, no serif or decorative typefaces.
